official.description: The Erasmus Trustfonds-TSH Changemaker Scholarship supports underrepresented students to pursue a master programme at Erasmus University Rotterdam, combining fee and living support with housing and a changemaker community. The Erasmus Trustfonds scholarship covers the statutory tuition fee and a monthly living allowance of EUR 600, while the TSH Changemaker Scholarship provides one year of housing in a Social Hub Residence. Erasmus MC states that, due to the limited number of scholarships available, it cannot offer a scholarship for every research master's programme and that the eligible programmes change each academic year.
official.program_type: Combined need- and merit-based Master's scholarship for underrepresented students at Erasmus MC, pairing an Erasmus Trustfonds grant with the TSH Changemaker Scholarship
official.english_requirement: The scholarship page sets no English test requirement of its own. Admission to the eligible Research Master's programmes requires sufficient command of the English language, satisfied by a qualifying English-language diploma (VWO with English, English-medium secondary education, four-year English-language higher vocational programme, or three-year English-language university degree) or by one of the following tests: IELTS 6.5 or higher with partial scores of minimally 6.0 (One Skill Retake accepted); internet-based TOEFL 90 or higher with partial scores of minimally 22; paper-based TOEFL 575 or higher with partial scores of minimally 57; Cambridge proficiency test level C1 or higher; LanguageCert Academic 70 or higher; Pearson PTE Academic 61 or higher

applicant_utility.summary: The award is EUR 9,895 for one academic year covering living costs and the statutory (EEA-rate) tuition fee, with EUR 600 of it paid monthly as a living allowance, plus a year of housing in a TSH Social Hub Residence through the Changemaker component. The published nationality rule is EEA, so non-EEA applicants should check the university-level version of this combined award, where nationality rules are stated per school. Only three full-time Research Master's programmes qualify - Health Sciences, Neuroscience and Molecular Medicine - and Erasmus MC explicitly warns that the funded programmes change each academic year, so confirm your programme is covered before building an application around this fund.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An EEA-national applicant with a bachelor average equivalent to Dutch 8.0 entering Health Sciences, Neuroscience or Molecular Medicine at Erasmus MC who belongs to a disadvantaged or underrepresented group and can evidence sustained community involvement.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your specific Research Master's programme is funded in the round you are applying for, since Erasmus MC states the eligible programmes change each academic year
Download the EUR budget plan template from the scholarship page and complete it in EUR before opening the OSIRIS case; the page says budget-plan questions must be asked before submitting
Convert all four documents to PDF and name each one studentnumber_lastname_name of document_name of scholarship
Draft the motivation letter against the five published questions, especially why you need the scholarship and how you will contribute to your country's social and economic development
Register the programme application through Studielink early enough that your student number exists before you open the scholarship case
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a Research Master's programme that is not funded in the current round, which Erasmus MC states happens because the number of scholarships is limited
Falling outside the EEA nationality rule stated on the Erasmus MC page
Submitting a grade list covering more than your highest degree, or a budget plan that is not on the official template
A motivation letter that argues academic excellence only, without the disadvantage, community-involvement and alumni-network commitment the page requires
Late submission caused by treating the scholarship deadline as later than the programme's own application deadline
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award pays the statutory tuition fee and EUR 600 per month, so anything above that - non-EU/EEA institutional tuition beyond the partial waiver, health insurance, visa and residence-permit costs, flights, books and the rest of a Rotterdam living budget - must be funded from other sources.
document_audit: Grade lists must cover only your highest degree; extra transcripts signal non-compliance with the page's instruction
The budget plan must use the provided EUR template only, and must show how you expect to cover all costs including the scholarship
A separate motivation letter is required for each scholarship you apply for, so budget writing time per award
All PDFs follow the prescribed naming format, which is a hard technical requirement of the portal

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the Research Master's programme through Studielink/Osiris, then open a case in the OSIRIS student portal ('Cases'), upload the four PDFs, and email the scholarship team beforehand with any budget-plan questions.

official.deadline_note: Leiden University publishes this as an annual recurring deadline - applications open 1 January and close 31 March at 23:59 CET each year - without naming a specific cycle year; 2027-03-31 is the next occurrence of that published rule. The Lutfia Rabbani Foundation's FAQ states the same window for the LUF-LRF scholarship.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle: applications open 1 January and close 31 March 23:59 CET, for the following academic year's intake
official.status_note: Leiden University states the deadline as '31 March 23:59 CET annually (applications open 1 January annually)'. The 2026 window has closed as of the verification date; the next window opens on 1 January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'EUR 30,000 for one academic year. The scholarship covers the tuition fee and housing fee (not the rent itself) of Leiden University. The small remaining amount is paid to the student in monthly installments.' Note: the above does not apply to LLM Advanced Studies programmes which have higher tuition fees.

official.description: The LUF - Lutfia Rabbani Scholarship Fund provides one scholarship annually to a master's student from an Arab country to attend a master's programme at Leiden University, on the basis of exceptional academic excellence and a strong motivation to promote Euro-Arab dialogue. The Lutfia Rabbani Foundation and the Leiden University Fund established the partnership in 2018 and renewed it on 21 February 2025, and the scholarship is strengthened by a mentoring programme offering personal and professional guidance. Leiden University states the award is EUR 30,000 for one academic year and is not a full scholarship.
official.program_type: Named scholarship fund for exceptional students from the Arab region, administered by Leiden University in partnership with the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation
official.english_requirement: Leiden University states that an English test is a prerequisite of admission to Leiden University and that the costs of the test must be covered by the applicant; the scholarship page sets no score threshold of its own. The Lutfia Rabbani Foundation does not require a separate English proficiency test in the scholarship application, since the official acceptance letter from the host university is taken as evidence of a sufficient level

applicant_utility.summary: This is EUR 30,000 for one academic year spent on Leiden's tuition fee and housing fee - the housing request fee, not the rent - with only a small residual reaching you in monthly instalments, and Leiden calls it explicitly 'not a full scholarship'. You must hold or be about to hold a Leiden admission letter: the Foundation advises applying to Leiden by 1 February for the September intake because admission decisions take 4-6 weeks and it cannot consider applicants without a letter of acceptance. One award is made per year to a national of one of the 18 listed Arab countries, and selection weighs academic excellence equally against financial need and motivation to promote Euro-Arab dialogue.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A national of one of the 18 listed Arab countries with an excellent academic record, a Leiden Master's admission letter (or an imminent one) and a credible commitment to Euro-Arab dialogue.
application_readiness_checklist: Get the Leiden admission application in early - by 1 February for the September intake - because processing takes 4-6 weeks and the Foundation cannot assess you without an acceptance letter
Draft the two-page motivation and purpose statement early, tying your field of study to Euro-Arab dialogue, personal and professional development, and impact in the local context
Line up two referees (academic or professional) who will sign in English, and tell the Foundation in advance if they will send references directly to scholarships@rabbanifoundation.org
Prepare a detailed programme outline of the intended Leiden Master's in English; the online university brochure is accepted if submitted as PDF
Complete the budget thoroughly - tuition fees, any other scholarship funds you have applied to, and expected expenses - since EUR 30,000 is a ceiling rather than a guarantee
Arrange passport copy, English translations of diplomas and transcripts, and separate proof of sufficient funds for the visa/residence permit
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a Leiden acceptance letter; the Foundation cannot consider such applications, so ask early whether a conditional letter will be accepted in your case
A motivation or purpose statement over two pages, or one that argues general excellence without Euro-Arab dialogue and local impact
Assuming EUR 30,000 covers everything - travel, rent and most living costs stay with you, and the visa proof-of-funds requirement sits on top of the award
Applying for an LLM Advanced Studies programme, which the award explicitly does not cover because of its higher tuition fees
Missing the 31 March 23:59 CET cut-off while waiting for a Leiden decision; the Foundation treats the date as fixed by the Selection Committee of its Board
Applying simultaneously for the Foundation's MSR Scholarship, which its FAQ reserves for students admitted to other Dutch universities
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to the Netherlands, the rent itself, health insurance, visa and residence-permit costs, and most day-to-day living expenses - Leiden requires separate proof of sufficient funds for the visa/residence permit, and the coverage excludes LLM Advanced Studies tuition.
document_audit: Degrees, diplomas and transcripts need English translations; an official statement of expected graduation is acceptable if you have not yet graduated
Two signed references are required, and referees may email them directly only if you inform the Foundation beforehand
The application form must be signed and dated; it is also downloadable inside the application portal
If your university cannot issue a PDF acceptance letter, a copy of the acceptance email is sufficient - keep the original email
Watch for the portal's submission confirmation email, which can land in your spam folder, and follow up with scholarships@rabbanifoundation.org if it does not arrive
alerts: The window runs from 1 January to 31 March 23:59 CET every year; as of the verification date the next window opens on 1 January 2027

A separate 'LUF - Lutfia Rabbani Scholarship Fund: Extra Gaza Scholarship' exists for Gazan students (deadline 23:59 on 31 March 2026, with no acceptance letter required) - do not confuse it with this award
Only one scholarship is awarded annually, it covers one academic year only, and a previous award does not guarantee renewal in a following year
The award cannot be combined with the Foundation's MSR Scholarship if you hold a Leiden acceptance letter, although combining it with funding from other sources is allowed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure the Leiden admission letter, complete the Foundation's signed application form, and upload the documents to the Foundation's online portal; the money is then routed either to Leiden as tuition or to you in instalments, with the Foundation's FAQ describing four equal instalments in September, December, March and June for the living-expenses route.
